mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate relative to its historical median compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and increasing the present value of S&P 500 index components, leading to positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (historical median) and the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points in the past three months signals labor market deterioration and economic slowdown, leading to negative 5-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months and the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an impending monetary tightening cycle, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative 60-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition (CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% MoM and FEDFUNDS > 2.5%) and the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In early-mid cycle expansion, rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening supply conditions and corporate profitability, leading to positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during early-mid cycle expansion (defined by INDPRO growth > 0.5% QoQ and UNRATE < 5.0%) and the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive 5-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average and the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained inflation rate exceeding 2.5% year-over-year (CPIAUCSL) signals an inflationary environment that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative 60-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with rising retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% MoM and RSAFS rises > 0.3% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% MoM and RSAFS rises > 0.3% MoM and the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase (declining unemployment rate), improving employment conditions support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive 5-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during labor market recovery (defined as UNRATE falling > 0.3pp in 3 months) and the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
